newsitem.title: UK: Ofwat makes progress on UK drought compensation.
newsitem.headline: Ofwat makes progress on UK drought compensation.

text.p: British water industry regulator Ofwat, the Office of Water Services, said on Monday it had made partial progress with its efforts to convince water suppliers to pay compensation for customers whose supplies are interrupted by drought at times when they are under a special drought order. After consultations since last June, Ofwat said in a statement that 13 companies had accepted proposed changes to their licences in order to formalise their offer to pay such compensation -- not required under existing water legislation.

However, another five large companies have accepted the proposals without agreeing to the amendment to their licences, while a further ten firms, including Yorkshire Water Plc, have only agreed to some of the proposals in principle and have yet to finalise their positions on compensation.

Yorkshire Water customers suffered extensive interruptions and cut-offs during 1995 when the region was the worst hit of many affected by droughts across Britain, and drought orders were issued widely across the country.

Ofwat director general Ian Byatt said in a statement that, in the case of the five companies that have not accepted the legally-binding change to their licence, "I do regret that on a matter of such potential importance they cannot agree to giving their intentions a formal status."

He also expressed disappointment at the ten undecided firms, saying, "the customers of these companies will be able to form their own opinion about the commitment to service demonstrated by their licenced water supplier. I am particularly concerned where a company's reluctance to accept my proposals is coupled with high leakage rates."

Firms signing up for the scheme agree to pay 10 stg per day to residential customers and 50 stg per day for business customers, with the maximum limited to the amount of charges paid by the customer in the preceding financial year.
